value.name: Miles confronts Ruth about Marilyn
value.description: Miles storms around Ruth's office, angrily questioning the bizarre sequence of Marilyn's marriages and divorces.
evidence: Ruth calmly watches Miles ranting around her office.

MILES
He divorced his wife -- he married
Marylin -- he divorced Marylin --
and he -- remarried his WIFE? What
kind of sick --

value.name: Ruth explains Marilyn had allies
value.description: Ruth reveals that Marilyn was friends with Howard and Amanda Doyle, who helped her because they dislike Miles's methods.
evidence:
RUTH
Marylin was friends with Howard and
Amanda Doyle. They don't like the
way you operate. They helped her.

value.name: Miles suspects a prenuptial agreement
value.description: Miles realizes that Howard never destroyed the prenuptial agreement and presses Ruth about whether Marilyn got money.
evidence:
MILES
He never ate the pre-nup, did he!

MILES
Did Marylin end up with money?

value.name: Ruth refuses to answer Miles
value.description: Ruth deflects Miles's questions, tells him to ask his wife, and assumes Marilyn signed the Massey prenup.
evidence:
RUTH
I have no idea what Howard Doyle eats. I'm not a damn dietician.

RUTH
She's YOUR wife. Why don't you ask
her? Anyway, I assume she signed the
highly over rated Massey pre-nup.

value.name: Miles admits he has no prenup
value.description: Miles reveals that he does not have a prenuptial agreement, and Ruth reacts with sympathy.
evidence:
MILES
I don't have a pre-nup
Miles hangs his head. Ruth sighs sympathetically.

value.name: Ruth mocks Miles with Shakespeare
value.description: Ruth tries to comfort Miles by quoting Shakespeare, but he rejects her patronizing tone and claims the line as his own material.
evidence:
RUTH
...The fault, dear Brutus, is not in
our stars...

MILES
Don't give me that crap. That's MY
crap.

value.name: Miles threatens Ruth with discipline
value.description: Frustrated, Miles threatens to have Ruth suspended and disbarred if she keeps withholding information.
evidence:
MILES
I'll have you suspended. I'll have
you disbarred.

RUTH
Don't threaten me, Miles. I did
nothing illegal.

value.name: Miles demands Marilyn's motive
value.description: Miles directly asks Ruth why Marilyn did what she did, seeking the motive behind her actions.
evidence:
MILES
...why did she do it, Ruth? Why?

value.name: Ruth invokes attorney-client privilege
value.description: Ruth refuses to reveal Marilyn's motive, citing attorney-client privilege and ending the exchange by returning to work.
evidence:
(As she goes back
into her work)
Sorry, Miles. But as a great and
clever man once said, What's good
for the goose --
